title: Map the lsp and list tools through the guard
action: oc-9's new registry-derived gate named two registered OpenCode tools that fall through bee-guard.ts's `default: return null` (a TypeScript-side allow): `lsp` — which returns file content for an arbitrary filePath, so it reaches the same material the secret-read guard exists to protect — and `list`. Map both onto the read-shaped write-guard payload the other read tools already use (write_guard/main.rs:66's is_read_tool family), so every registered read- or write-capable tool asks bee. Then remove them from discovery.md's named-gap list and update the hook table. The registry gate in packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/tests/opencode_plugin_contracts.rs must go green by mapping the tools, never by widening the gate's allow-list — if a tool genuinely should not be gated, that is a named exclusion with a written reason, not a silent skip. SCOPE WIDENED (orchestrator, after the first attempt blocked correctly): the suite's opencode_call_fixture payload table now needs one row per newly mapped tool id — add the lsp and list rows there, DATA ROWS ONLY, never a change to assertion logic or to the gates' derivation. Prior attempt left both tool mappings and the discovery.md updates in the working tree uncommitted; verify them rather than redoing them blind.
